title: Smithfield budget board questions FY2026 revenue and spending figures

← Back to the wire
Government
Smithfield budget board questions FY2026 revenue and spending figures
Board members pressed a finance official over discrepancies in reported revenue totals, with one figure cited as $97,51,235 and another overage described as roughly $1,22694.
The Smithfield Budget and Financial Review Board met Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, and reviewed fiscal year 2026 tentative and final budget figures, with members questioning discrepancies in the numbers presented.
THE NUMBERS Mr. Suza, presenting the agenda item, said expenditures were "96,67 32" and that the town "overextended it by 1,22694," but also "brought in 97, 97,51,235" in revenue, which he said was more than had been budgeted. Confusion followed over how the revenue figures were derived, with one board member saying, "That's why I specifically asked for those numbers."
DISPUTED FIGURES A board member pressed on inconsistencies between numbers sent earlier and those presented at the meeting, saying, "So your 95 was 97 was how is that?" Mr. Suza responded by referencing an updated document, saying, "I sent you an updated brand and it has 97,000 right at the bottom."
FUND BALANCE A board member raised the question of whether the reported surplus reflected draw-downs on the fund balance or reserve fund, asking "is it still that when you account for um draw downs on the fund balance on the reserve fund as part of why your budget cut down." The same member said he wanted to examine how much of the reported revenue was nonrecurring, saying, "What we're what we're going to want to look at though is see what what of that is revenue that is nonrecurring revenue."
NEXT STEPS The board asked for the latest Excel file to be sent for comparison purposes. A board member said of the figures, "I think that's that leaves us in a a lot better place," pending the additional data.
Fund balance was also discussed later in the meeting regarding the FY2027 budget process, when a board member noted that a prior analysis showed the town's fund balance stood at "the month three days" versus the two months it is "supposed to be at."
